title: Compressing the long-range Ewald Coulomb branch is done by rotating/recombining the auxiliary basis at initialization, not by rotating the Coulomb matrix
symptom: Work on the moment/Ewald long-range compression was repeatedly described as 'rotating the Coulomb matrix' / 'rotate V'. The implementation actually performs an orthogonal rotation/recombination of the auxiliary basis during initialization and stores a reordered long-range prefix block; the matrix is only represented in the rotated auxiliary basis.
root_cause: The long-range Ewald branch enters the auxiliary basis only through multipole moments, so the exact reformulation is: rotate/recombine the auxiliary basis inside each (type, L) subspace so the multipole moment lives in one representative channel, then reorder those channels to the prefix — giving full short-range + reduced-prefix long-range. There is no Coulomb-matrix rotation involved. The rotation must happen at the very beginning of EXX initialization so that the rest of the calculation is unchanged.
minimal_fix: Implement the rotation on the auxiliary basis at EXX initialization (as in the RSH-functional Ewald rotation already merged into the ri-moment branch) and describe it as 'auxiliary-basis rotation and prefix reordering'; keep the downstream Coulomb/chi0/Wc code path untouched.
validation: On a fixed case (e.g. the SiC sg15 shrink test) dump the complete Coulomb eigenvalue list — the LibRPA non-singular and full prints 'The largest/smallest eigenvalue of Coulomb matrix(non-singular)' and 'The 1st/2nd/3rd/-1th eigenvalue of Coulomb matrix(Full)' — before and after the rotation and require the non-singular spectrum to be unchanged apart from the intended long-range prefix compression; also confirm RPA/GW results are unchanged versus the unrotated run.
avoid: Do not implement or describe the scheme as rotating the Coulomb matrix / the Coulomb potential itself, and do not combine the rotation with changes elsewhere in the Coulomb path — the reformulation is exact only if downstream stays identical.
